scenes.tts: What happens to a synapse when the brake on its own protein making is gone?
scenes.visual: Title card: Too Much Protein. The recurring synapse, with ribosomes in the dendrite and a brake icon on them.
scenes.narration: What happens to a synapse when the brake on its own protein making is gone?

scenes.tts: Fragile X syndrome is the most common inherited cause of intellectual disability.
scenes.visual: An X chromosome with a narrow gap near its tip. Label: fragile X syndrome.
scenes.narration: Fragile X syndrome is the most common inherited cause of intellectual disability.

scenes.tts: Its cause is a three-base repeat, C G G, near the start of the F M R one gene.
scenes.caption: Its cause is a three-base repeat, CGG, near the start of the FMR1 gene.
scenes.visual: A gene strip labelled FMR1 with C G G units stacked near its start.
scenes.narration: Its cause is a three-base repeat, CGG, near the start of the FMR1 gene.

scenes.tts: Above about two hundred copies, the gene is usually silenced.
scenes.caption: Above about 200 copies, the gene is usually silenced.
scenes.visual: A repeat counter climbs past 45, through 55 to 200 (premutation), then past 200. The control region turns grey: methylated.
scenes.narration: Above about 200 copies, the gene is usually silenced.

scenes.tts: So little or no F M R P is made. It binds R N A and holds back translation.
scenes.caption: So little or no FMRP is made. It binds RNA and holds back translation.
scenes.visual: FMRP travels with messenger R N As in a dendrite, holding them back from ribosomes.
scenes.narration: So little or no FMRP is made. It binds RNA and holds back translation.

scenes.tts: Dendrites carry their own ribosomes, so synapses can make protein within minutes. F M R P is a brake on that.
scenes.caption: Dendrites carry their own ribosomes, so synapses can make protein within minutes. FMRP is a brake on that.
scenes.visual: Ribosomes beside a synapse start making protein after a signal; a stopwatch shows minutes. The brake icon returns.
scenes.narration: Dendrites carry their own ribosomes, so synapses can make protein within minutes. FMRP is a brake on that.

scenes.tts: One signal that releases the brake comes through a glutamate receptor, M glue R five.
scenes.caption: One signal that releases the brake comes through a glutamate receptor, mGluR5.
scenes.visual: Glutamate binds a receptor on the dendrite labelled mGluR5; the brake lifts.
scenes.narration: One signal that releases the brake comes through a glutamate receptor, mGluR5.

scenes.tts: In hippocampal slices, activating that class of receptor makes synapses weaken for hours. This long-term depression normally needs new protein.
scenes.visual: A response trace that drops and stays down for hours. Label: long-term depression, hippocampal slices. Blocking translation: an early dip, then recovery to baseline.
scenes.narration: In hippocampal slices, activating that class of receptor makes synapses weaken for hours. This long-term depression normally needs new protein.

scenes.tts: Predict. Take the brake away. What happens to that weakening? And does it still need new protein?
scenes.visual: Text on screen: Predict. Knockout trace, unknown. Needs new protein?
scenes.narration: Predict. Take the brake away. What happens to that weakening? And does it still need new protein?

scenes.tts: In fragile X mice, the weakening is exaggerated. Later work found it no longer needs new protein.
scenes.visual: Knockout trace dips further than typical. Blocking translation no longer stops the drop.
scenes.narration: In fragile X mice, the weakening is exaggerated. Later work found it no longer needs new protein.

scenes.tts: Normally, the weakening waits for new protein. Without the brake, the usual reading goes, that protein is already there in excess.
scenes.visual: Split panel. Typical: the dendrite waits for a burst of new protein before the trace stays down. Knockout: protein already piled up, the trace drops at once. Label: the usual reading.
scenes.narration: Normally, the weakening waits for new protein. Without the brake, the usual reading goes, that protein is already there in excess.

scenes.tts: In two thousand four, Bear, Huber and Warren proposed the M glue R theory.
scenes.caption: In 2004, Bear, Huber and Warren proposed the mGluR theory.
scenes.visual: Credit: Bear, Huber and Warren, 2004. Card: the mGluR theory.
scenes.narration: In 2004, Bear, Huber and Warren proposed the mGluR theory.

scenes.tts: Without F M R P, the receptor drives too much protein synthesis, and many features follow.
scenes.caption: Without FMRP, the receptor drives too much protein synthesis, and many features follow.
scenes.visual: An arrow from mGluR5 to a large pile of protein, then to a row of traits.
scenes.narration: Without FMRP, the receptor drives too much protein synthesis, and many features follow.

scenes.tts: Predict. If too much receptor signalling causes the traits, what should halving the receptor do?
scenes.visual: Text on screen: Predict. A cross: fragile X mouse times a mouse with one working receptor gene.
scenes.narration: Predict. If too much receptor signalling causes the traits, what should halving the receptor do?

scenes.tts: In two thousand seven, Gool Durlen and Bear bred fragile X mice with one working copy of the receptor gene.
scenes.caption: In 2007, Gül Dölen and Bear bred fragile X mice with one working copy of the receptor gene.
scenes.visual: Credit: Dölen and Bear, 2007. The cross produces a double-mutant mouse.
scenes.narration: In 2007, Gül Dölen and Bear bred fragile X mice with one working copy of the receptor gene.

scenes.tts: Protein synthesis, spine density and sound-triggered seizures all moved toward typical.
scenes.visual: Three bars, protein synthesis, spine density and sound-triggered seizures, each move from the knockout level back toward typical.
scenes.narration: Protein synthesis, spine density and sound-triggered seizures all moved toward typical.

scenes.tts: Halving the receptor shows the two genes interact. It may be part of the cause, or it may offset the defect another way.
scenes.visual: Two labelled readings side by side: part of the cause; offsets the defect by another route.
scenes.narration: Halving the receptor shows the two genes interact. It may be part of the cause, or it may offset the defect another way.

scenes.tts: Now a different late test, with a drug. In adult fragile X mice, chronic treatment with a receptor blocker corrected many traits.
scenes.visual: A separate panel, not the chapter-one grid. Panel label: adult drug: turns down mGluR5 signalling, does not replace FMRP. Label: tests whether the circuit can still be adjusted. Credit: Michalon and colleagues, 2012.
scenes.narration: Now a different late test, with a drug. In adult fragile X mice, chronic treatment with a receptor blocker corrected many traits.

scenes.tts: So in mice, the circuit could still be adjusted after it was built. The drug does not put F M R P back.
scenes.visual: The adult mouse's trait bars move toward typical. Note on the panel: does not restore FMRP.
scenes.narration: So in mice, the circuit could still be adjusted after it was built. The drug does not put FMRP back.
scenes.caption: So in mice, the circuit could still be adjusted after it was built. The drug does not put FMRP back.

scenes.tts: Drugs like this were already being tested in people. Trials in adolescents and adults showed no benefit over placebo on the main measures.
scenes.visual: Outcome card: no benefit over placebo on the main measures. Labels: mavoglurant, 2016; basimglurant, 2018.
scenes.narration: Drugs like this were already being tested in people. Trials in adolescents and adults showed no benefit over placebo on the main measures.

scenes.tts: A later trial in young children also found no benefit over placebo.
scenes.visual: A second outcome card. Label: young children, no benefit over placebo.
scenes.narration: A later trial in young children also found no benefit over placebo.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: a mouse rescue tests a mechanism, not a cure.
scenes.visual: Closing card: mouse rescue: yes. Human trials so far: no benefit over placebo.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: a mouse rescue tests a mechanism, not a cure.
